dialogues.speaker: Uturunku
dialogues.text: Do you get... scared?

dialogues.speaker: Tepoz
dialogues.text: Traveler, can I ask you a favor?

dialogues.speaker: Tepoz
dialogues.text: My mother's a doctor. When she heard about the attacks in the wilderness, she rushed out to help, and I haven't heard from her since.

dialogues.speaker: Tepoz
dialogues.text: I'm worried. She's not a fighter, and I can't leave to check on her. I want her to stay out of this, so if you see her, can you please tell her to take shelter?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course! We've got this!

dialogues.speaker: Tepoz
dialogues.text: Thank you. That makes it easier to focus on the current battle.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's normal to be afraid.

dialogues.speaker: Uturunku
dialogues.text: Normal? You mean... I'm not being a coward?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Not at all! You're here, aren't you? Ready to fight even despite your fear! That's impressive!

dialogues.speaker: Uturunku
dialogues.text: Oh... Y—Yeah! You're right! Thanks, you two.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not really.

dialogues.speaker: Uturunku
dialogues.text: I... I knew it. You're too strong for that...

dialogues.speaker: Uturunku
dialogues.text: *sigh*...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Doctor... Wait, do you know Tepoz?

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: He's my son... Why? Did something happen to him?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, no! He's fine! He's just worried about you. He asked us to tell you to seek shelter.

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: Ah, I see. I know it's dangerous to be out and about like this, but I just can't sit back and do nothing...

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: How about this... I'll write to him and promise to team up with the next group of warriors I come across. I'll be safer that way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds good! Paimon's sure he'll be relieved you're okay.

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: Thank you for passing along his message.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Absolutely.

dialogues.speaker: Uturunku
dialogues.text: That's what I'm hoping for, too, it's just... Never mind.

dialogues.speaker: Raman
dialogues.text: Uh... Ugh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Someone's injured... That must be the messenger! Hey, are you alright? Can you still walk?

dialogues.speaker: Raman
dialogues.text: The battle report, I have to find the battle report...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We already found it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, we got you covered! Here you go.

dialogues.speaker: Raman
dialogues.text: Oh, thank you... *sigh* I just hope I'm not too late...

dialogues.speaker: Raman
dialogues.text: In times like these, every second counts. Even a short delay can put lives at risk...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry about that! We can take things from here. You just need to head back to the Stadium and focus on getting better.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Have faith in your people.

dialogues.speaker: Raman
dialogues.text: ...You're right. I can't do much else in my current state anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How can we make sure he'll safely get back, though? We can't let him make the journey alone, it's too dangerous out there...

dialogues.speaker: Brave Yumkasaur
dialogues.text: Roar... roar, roar...

dialogues.speaker: Raman
dialogues.text: Huh? What the...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Looks like this yumkasaur wants to give you a lift.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... you guys sure about this? It's really dangerous out there...

dialogues.speaker: Brave Yumkasaur
dialogues.text: Roar, roar...

dialogues.speaker: Raman
dialogues.text: Alright, well... Thanks, this is a huge help.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Be careful on the road.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Thank goodness for those saurians. They really came to the rescue.

choices.text: Yeah. He stands a much better chance of survival now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's no wonder people from Natlan are so fond of their saurian companions.

choices.text: Turns out they could understand what you were saying this whole time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really, that's your takeaway from this? Unbelievable...

dialogues.speaker: Stadukhin
dialogues.text: The Captain must have known the situation would get a lot more dire than expected. That would explain why he was so anxious.

dialogues.speaker: Chimalli
dialogues.text: Thanks to you, we managed to clear out the threats in the surrounding area. Let's head back.

dialogues.speaker: Awhina
dialogues.text: I want to seek shelter as well, but the People of the Springs need these potions. I have to get them there.

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: It really is getting dangerous out here. Looks like sticking with a group of warriors is the only way to stay safe...

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: Anyway, I should head out. Other places need my attention.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She seems quite anxious... Guess that means things aren't looking good...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Fatui could escort you?

dialogues.speaker: Awhina
dialogues.text: Uh... I'm not sure about that.

dialogues.speaker: Stadukhin
dialogues.text: We can get you close. It's on our way.

dialogues.speaker: Awhina
dialogues.text: Oh, well... Great! I appreciate it!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I wouldn't risk it.

dialogues.speaker: Awhina
dialogues.text: You're right. It's dangerous out here. I don't even know if I'd make it...

dialogues.speaker: Awhina
dialogues.text: Other caravans are already there, so it should be fine.

dialogues.speaker: Kamaka
dialogues.text: How long are these attacks going to last...

dialogues.speaker: Kamaka
dialogues.text: I was heading to the People of the Springs for business, but looks like I can kiss that Mora goodbye. At least I'm still in one piece.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did something happen on the road?

dialogues.speaker: Kamaka
dialogues.text: I was attacked by monsters. I really thought it was over, but would you believe it... the Fatui saved my life.

dialogues.speaker: Kamaka
dialogues.text: The Captain's soldiers running around Natlan rescuing people... I almost couldn't believe it. I guess the Abyss really is our common enemy.

dialogues.speaker: Kamaka
dialogues.text: They set out again after rescuing us. I hope they'll be okay out there.

dialogues.speaker: Kamaka
dialogues.text: Hey, you two! We made it back in one piece!

dialogues.speaker: Kamaka
dialogues.text: Honestly, it's all thanks to you.

dialogues.speaker: Kamaka
dialogues.text: The Fatui that helped us are still fighting out there. I hope they're okay.

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: Oh, I didn't expect to see you here.

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: I heard medical personnel were needed at the Stadium, so I followed a group of warriors back here.

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: My age means I can't charge to the frontlines, but I can handle things here. Everything will get better.

dialogues.speaker: Awhina
dialogues.text: I've decided to bring these supplies to the Stadium, but this amount won't nearly be enough. There's a shortage pretty much everywhere.

dialogues.speaker: Awhina
dialogues.text: We have emergency stockpiles of things like water, food, and medicine, but what if we'll need them even more in the future...?

dialogues.speaker: Awhina
dialogues.text: Guess I'll just have to talk to my guild, and see if they've got any more to spare.

dialogues.speaker: Ardra
dialogues.text: It's you two! I'm so glad you're alright!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! You made it back!

dialogues.speaker: Kokpon
dialogues.text: Sure did. Dargo made sure we got back safely before rushing out again.

dialogues.speaker: Ardra
dialogues.text: Plus, we managed to deliver the medical supplies to the Stadium. I really can't thank you enough for your help!

dialogues.speaker: Diligent Yumkasaur
dialogues.text: No going outside. It's too dangerous. That goes for you too!

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you two! Perfect timing! I heard you saved this lady, too.

dialogues.speaker: Awhina
dialogues.text: That's right! They rescued my potion shipment.

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: Wonderful, these potions are just what I needed to treat my patients. I'll make sure you're well rewarded for the trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Awhina
dialogues.text: Don't worry about it. The regular price is more than enough. Time is the most precious thing right now.

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: Thank you so much! Let's head out soon.

dialogues.speaker: Awhina
dialogues.text: Sounds good.

dialogues.speaker: Uturunku
dialogues.text: I've managed to accept my fear, but I still want to ask you one last thing... If I die, do you think anyone will remember me?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't think about that. Do your best to stay alive.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! Please do whatever you can to stay alive! Your life is super important!

dialogues.speaker: Uturunku
dialogues.text: My life... is super important...

dialogues.speaker: Uturunku
dialogues.text: ...Got it. Thank you again for leading me to the answer.

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: Thank you. *sigh* They really came out of nowhere...

dialogues.speaker: Guaman
dialogues.text: Yeah, that was close. Thank you for coming all this way to help us, Doctor.

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: Just doing my part.

dialogues.speaker: Chimalli
dialogues.text: Ah, by the way... I think I know where some monsters might be. It's an area nearby.

dialogues.speaker: Chimalli
dialogues.text: If you've got some time, I'd appreciate the back-up.

choices.text: Sorry, I have something else to do.

response.speaker: Chimalli
response.text: Don't worry about it. I'll round up a few warriors to go with me.

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: Oh, I didn't expect to see you here.

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: My son wrote back to me and said things are under control on his end. That's one less thing to worry about for now.

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: I heard medical personnel were needed at the Stadium, so I followed a group of warriors back here.

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: My age means I can't charge to the frontlines, but I can handle things here. Everything will get better.

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: Still no sign of any warriors. I need to head out soon. We're running out of time...

dialogues.speaker: Tepoz
dialogues.text: I'll be heading out with the others soon. *sigh* I just hope she's okay...

dialogues.speaker: Uturunku
dialogues.text: *sigh*... I have to do this.

dialogues.speaker: Uturunku
dialogues.text: Thanks for your encouragement. You helped me accept my fear, and now... It doesn't seem so scary anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Guaman
dialogues.text: That doctor is amazing! I owe her my life. I'll never forget that!

dialogues.speaker: Chimalli
dialogues.text: We'll continue to stand guard. Thanks for all the help.

dialogues.speaker: Awhina
dialogues.text: I... I suppose our safety is in your hands, then.

dialogues.speaker: Stadukhin
dialogues.text: It's dangerous to rely solely on others. You also need to look after your own safety.

dialogues.speaker: Awhina
dialogues.text: At least we weren't the only caravan headed to the People of the Springs. I'll focus on doing what I can while staying safe.

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: Oh, that reminds me, is it possible to set up some future deliveries?

dialogues.speaker: Awhina
dialogues.text: I'm not sure... Communication is tricky right now, and our stock is getting low, but I can try.

dialogues.speaker: Uturunku
dialogues.text: I don't have to die to become a hero. Just being remembered is enough.

dialogues.speaker: Uturunku
dialogues.text: You're right. We're not fighting to die. We're fighting to survive.
